text: Okay, so I want you to um refactor the auth middleware. Right now it checks the token on every request, and that's like a database hit each time. Can you add a small in-memory cache with a five minute TTL? Keep the existing tests passing, and uh add one test for the expiry case. Don't touch the login handler, it's fine as it is.

So the Docker build is really slow, it takes like eight minutes on CI. I think it's because we copy the whole repo before running npm install, so the layer cache never hits. Can you, um, can you reorder the Dockerfile so that package.json and the lock file get copied first, then install, then copy the rest? Also switch the base image to node twenty slim if that doesn't break anything.

I need a regex that matches the version tags in our changelog. They look like v, then a major number, a dot, a minor number, a dot, and a patch number, and sometimes there's a dash and like beta or rc with a number after it. Um, it should not match dates, so twenty twenty six dash ten dash twenty four should fail. Write it for Python and add three or four test strings.

Hey, quick update on the flaky test. So it's the one in the payments suite that times out maybe one in ten runs. I looked at the logs and it's not the test itself, it's the mock server, it takes too long to start up on the GitHub runners. I'm going to add a health check before the tests start, and if that doesn't fix it by Thursday, I'll just bump the timeout from thirty to sixty seconds and move on.

So for standup, yesterday I finished the migration script and um I got it reviewed by Priya. Today I'm going to run it against staging, and if the row counts match, I'll schedule the production run for Monday night. The only blocker is, uh, I still don't have write access to the prod replica, so if someone on infra can grant that, that'd be great. Oh and I'll be out Friday afternoon.

Can you write unit tests for the date parser in utils slash time dot ts? I want coverage for ISO strings, for Unix timestamps in seconds and in milliseconds, and for the weird format the legacy API sends, which is like day slash month slash year with a two digit year. Um, use the existing test helpers, don't add any new dependencies. And if you find a bug while you're at it, don't fix it yet, just leave a comment and tell me.

I went through the pull request. Overall it looks good, but I have a few things. First, the retry loop doesn't have a max, so if the upstream is down it'll just spin forever. Can we cap it at like five attempts with exponential backoff? Second, the error messages are logging the full request body, which might include tokens, so let's not do that. And third, uh, the new endpoint isn't in the OpenAPI spec yet. Once those are fixed I'm happy to approve.

Alright, so our hackathon project is basically a tool that watches your terminal and when a command fails, it suggests a fix. Um, it runs fully on device, so nothing leaves your laptop. We built it in Swift and it uses the on-device model for the suggestions. The demo is going to be like two minutes: I'll break a git rebase on purpose, and then show it recovering. We still need someone to make the slides, and uh we should rehearse at least twice before four o'clock.

The pods keep getting OOM killed in the staging cluster. Can you look at the deployment yaml and, um, figure out if the memory limit is too low? I think it's set to five hundred twelve megabytes, but the JVM heap alone is configured for like four hundred. So there's basically no headroom. Suggest new requests and limits, but don't apply anything with kubectl, just give me the diff and I'll apply it myself after the incident review.

So I've been thinking about the onboarding flow and honestly I think we're asking for too much up front. Like, we ask for the email, then the team name, then we ask them to invite people, and then there's the integrations screen, and by that point a lot of people just leave. I looked at the funnel and we lose about forty percent between the invite step and the integrations step. What if we just skip the invite step entirely and let people do it later from settings? I mean, we'd lose some invites probably, but I think more people would actually finish. And we could add a little banner on the dashboard that reminds them to invite their team after like a day or two. I don't know, it's worth an experiment at least. Maybe we run it for two weeks on half the new signups and see what happens to activation. I can write up a short doc on it tomorrow if people think it's a good idea.

Okay, here's what I need. We're migrating the notification service from the old queue to the new event bus. Um, the old code is in services slash notify and it uses a polling loop that checks the queue every two seconds. The new event bus pushes messages, so we can drop the polling entirely. Step one, add a subscriber that listens on the notifications topic. Step two, move the message handling out of the polling loop into a function that both paths can call, so we can run them side by side for a while. Step three, add a feature flag, call it use event bus, default off. Don't delete the old polling code yet, we need it as a fallback until we've run both for a week. Also, the handler has to be idempotent because the event bus can deliver the same message twice. Uh, use the message ID for deduplication, and keep the dedupe window at like ten minutes. Write tests for the duplicate case and for the flag being off. When you're done, give me a short summary of what changed and anything you weren't sure about.

Bueno, necesito que revises el script de despliegue. Eh, ahora mismo tarda como diez minutos porque construye la imagen de Docker desde cero cada vez. ¿Puedes hacer que use la caché de capas? Y otra cosa, no cambies las variables de entorno de producción, eso lo hago yo el lunes.

Hola a todos, una actualización rápida. El servidor de pruebas estuvo caído casi dos horas anoche por un problema con el certificado. Ya lo renové y añadí una alerta para que nos avise treinta días antes de que caduque. Eh, si alguien ve errores raros esta mañana, avísenme por favor.
えーと、昨日のデプロイの件なんですけど、ステージングでは問題なかったんですが、本番で二回タイムアウトが出ました。原因はたぶんデータベースの接続数の上限だと思います。今日中に設定を確認して、金曜日までに修正を出します。
